name: Al-Farazdaq
bio: Hammam ibn Ghalib came from a Tamimi family in Basra. In his long exchange of satires with Jarir, each poet answered in his rival’s metre and rhyme, calling on the remembered battles and genealogies of their tribes. Grammarians and lexicographers often cited his verse. Al-Zirikli records that he granted protection to people who took refuge at the grave of his father Ghalib, himself remembered for his generosity. Al-Farazdaq died in Basra in 110 AH (728 CE).
